facts.text: Accidents have three severity bands: fatalities (deaths), serious injuries causing lost working time or permanent harm, and property damage to machines, vehicles or structures without anyone being hurt.
facts.quote: A fatality is a death. A serious injury causes lost working time or permanent harm, and agencies define it differently (lost-time injury, reportable injury, high-potential incident). Property damage is harm to machines, vehicles or structures with no one hurt.

facts.text: Accident records become thinner and less reliable as accident severity decreases.
facts.quote: the records get thinner and less reliable as severity goes down.

facts.text: Agencies define serious injury differently, using categories such as lost-time injury, reportable injury and high-potential incident.
facts.quote: agencies define it differently (lost-time injury, reportable injury, high-potential incident).

facts.text: Only deaths are investigated and published case by case.
facts.quote: Only deaths are investigated and published case by case.

facts.text: Accident databases record fatalities far better than property-only collisions, near misses, nuisance alarms or events prevented by operators.
facts.quote: Accident databases record fatalities far better than property-only collisions, near misses, nuisance alarms or events the operator prevented [Chapter 4].

facts.text: In US mining in 2025, powered haulage caused 13 of 33 deaths and 426 of 4,792 nonfatal injuries.

facts.text: In US construction in 2020, struck-by incidents caused 150 deaths and 14,000 nonfatal injuries, with 1.4 billion dollars in direct compensation costs.

facts.text: The collision mitigation system is intended to prevent fatalities, serious injuries and property damage, but the evidence for selecting tests is strongest for deaths.
facts.quote: The system is meant to prevent all three bands, but the evidence for what to test is strongest for deaths.

facts.text: The booklet recommends using fatality patterns to prioritize scenarios and treating frequency and damage estimates as much weaker evidence.
